config.title: Build correlation ID middleware

intro.title: Build correlation ID middleware
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a correlation ID middleware for a Node.js Express application. You will learn how to generate a unique identifier for each incoming HTTP request and attach it to the request object for tracking purposes. The core programming concept involves middleware functions, which intercept and process requests in a pipeline. You will use key technologies like Express.js, the `uuid` library for ID generation, and HTTP headers. By the end, you'll have a functional middleware that logs correlation IDs to help debug and trace requests across services.
intro.usecase: Correlation IDs are essential in distributed systems like microservices architectures, where a single user request might trigger multiple services. In e-commerce platforms, when a customer places an order, correlation IDs help track the request through inventory checks, payment processing, and shipping services. This allows developers to trace errors across service boundaries in monitoring dashboards like Datadog or New Relic. Without correlation IDs, debugging production issues would be like finding a needle in a haystack across dozens of interconnected services.

objectives: Implement a middleware function that generates a unique correlation ID for incoming HTTP requests
Apply the correlation ID to the request object for use in subsequent middleware and route handlers
Configure the middleware to check for existing correlation IDs in request headers and reuse them when present
Integrate the correlation ID middleware into an Express application using app.use()
Manipulate response headers to include the correlation ID for client-side tracking
Construct a logging mechanism that includes the correlation ID in all log entries for request tracing
Initialize a test endpoint that demonstrates the correlation ID flow through the middleware chain

steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: At the top of your middleware file, import the crypto module and the uuid package (v4).
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import Node.js built-in modules and npm packages.
steps.seedCode:
// Import crypto and uuid here

// Your middleware code will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: The crypto module and uuid package are imported and ready to use for generating correlation IDs.
successCriteria: crypto and uuid are imported using require() statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the required modules. The crypto module provides random ID generation capabilities, and uuid gives us a standardized alternative for creating unique identifiers.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both modules: crypto (built-in) and uuid (npm package).
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import two modules: crypto (Node.js built-in) and uuid (npm package). Use require() statements at the top of your file.

steps.title: Create the middleware function structure
steps.instruction: Define a function named correlationIdMiddleware that takes three parameters: req, res, and next.
steps.hint: Create a function with the exact name correlationIdMiddleware that accepts three parameters in order.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named correlationIdMiddleware is created with the correct parameter signature.
successCriteria: Function correlationIdMiddleware is defined with req, res, and next parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the middleware function structure correctly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function is named exactly correlationIdMiddleware and takes three parameters: req, res, and next.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check the name and parameter order.

steps.title: Check for existing correlation ID in request headers
steps.instruction: Inside the correlationIdMiddleware function, check if the incoming request has a 'x-correlation-id' header.
steps.hint: Access request headers using req.headers and check if 'x-correlation-id' exists.
steps.expectedOutcome: The middleware function now includes logic to check for an existing correlation ID in the request headers.
successCriteria: The correlationIdMiddleware function contains a conditional check for the 'x-correlation-id' header in req.headers.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the header check. This is essential for determining whether to use an existing correlation ID or generate a new one.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're checking specifically for the 'x-correlation-id' header in the request headers object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The header check is missing or incorrect. Remember to access req.headers and check for the 'x-correlation-id' key.

steps.title: Generate a new correlation ID if none exists
steps.instruction: Inside the correlationIdMiddleware function, after checking for the header, add an if statement that generates a new correlation ID using crypto.randomUUID() when no header exists.
steps.hint: Use an if statement to check if the correlation ID is falsy, then assign crypto.randomUUID() to a variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The middleware will now generate a unique correlation ID when the request doesn't have one in headers.
successCriteria: An if statement checks if correlationId is falsy and assigns crypto.randomUUID() to a variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the logic to generate a new correlation ID when needed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to use crypto.randomUUID() inside an if statement that checks if correlationId is falsy.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the middleware, after getting the header, add an if statement that generates a new ID using crypto.randomUUID() when no header exists.

steps.title: Store the correlation ID in the request object
steps.instruction: Inside your correlationIdMiddleware function, attach the correlationId variable to the request object as req.correlationId.
steps.hint: You can assign the correlationId value to a property on the req object. This makes it available for other middleware and route handlers.
steps.expectedOutcome: The correlation ID value is attached to the request object so it can be accessed later in the request lifecycle.
successCriteria: The req.correlationId property is assigned the correlationId value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully attached the correlation ID to the request object. This will allow other parts of your application to access it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're assigning the correlationId variable to req.correlationId inside the middleware function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The correlation ID needs to be stored on the request object. Try adding req.correlationId = correlationId; inside your middleware function.

steps.title: Set the correlation ID in response headers
steps.instruction: Inside your correlationIdMiddleware function, after storing the correlation ID in the request object, set the 'x-correlation-id' header on the response object using res.setHeader().
steps.hint: Use res.setHeader('x-correlation-id', correlationId) to add the correlation ID to the response headers.
steps.expectedOutcome: The middleware will now add the correlation ID to the response headers, making it available to downstream services.
successCriteria: The correlationIdMiddleware function includes res.setHeader('x-correlation-id', correlationId) before calling next().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the correlation ID to the response headers. This ensures the ID is passed along the request chain.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using res.setHeader() with the correct header name and correlation ID value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The response header wasn't set correctly. Check that you're using res.setHeader('x-correlation-id', correlationId) before calling next().

steps.title: Call next() to continue middleware chain
steps.instruction: Inside your correlationIdMiddleware function, call next() at the end to pass control to the next middleware in the chain.
steps.hint: Add the call to next() after you've set the response header, but before the function ends.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your middleware function will now properly pass control to the next middleware after processing the correlation ID.
successCriteria: The correlationIdMiddleware function includes a call to next() at the end of its execution.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! Calling next() ensures your middleware doesn't block the request pipeline and allows subsequent middleware or route handlers to execute.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling next() inside your middleware function. Remember that next() should be called after you've finished processing the correlation ID.
steps.feedbackWrong: It looks like you haven't added the call to next(). Without calling next(), the request will hang and never reach subsequent middleware or route handlers.

steps.title: Export the middleware function
steps.instruction: Export the correlationIdMiddleware function using module.exports so it can be imported in other files.
steps.hint: Use module.exports to make your function available outside this file. This is the standard CommonJS export pattern in Node.js.
steps.expectedOutcome: The middleware function is exported and ready to be imported and used in an Express application.
successCriteria: The correlationIdMiddleware function is exported using module.exports.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the middleware function. It can now be imported and used in other parts of your application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using module.exports to export the correlationIdMiddleware function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The export is missing or incorrect. Use module.exports to export the correlationIdMiddleware function.

steps.title: Import the middleware in your main app file
steps.instruction: In your main Express app file (e.g., app.js or index.js), import the correlationIdMiddleware using require().
steps.hint: Use require() with the correct path to the middleware file. If the middleware is in the same directory, use './correlationIdMiddleware'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing a custom module
const myMiddleware = require('./myMiddleware');
steps.expectedOutcome: The correlationIdMiddleware is successfully imported into the main app file, ready to be used as middleware.
successCriteria: correlationIdMiddleware is imported using require() with the correct path.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the middleware. Now it's ready to be used in your Express app.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the import uses require() and the correct path to the middleware file.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import is missing or incorrect. Use require() to import correlationIdMiddleware from its file.

steps.title: Use the middleware in your Express app
steps.instruction: Add the correlationIdMiddleware to your Express app using app.use() before your routes.
steps.hint: Call app.use() with correlationIdMiddleware as the argument. Place it after the import comment and before any route definitions.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: using middleware in Express
app.use(express.json());
steps.expectedOutcome: The correlationIdMiddleware is now applied globally to all routes in your Express app.
successCriteria: app.use(correlationIdMiddleware) is added before the app.listen call.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the correlation ID middleware to your Express app. It will now process every incoming request.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using app.use() with correlationIdMiddleware as the argument, placed before app.listen().
steps.feedbackWrong: The middleware isn't properly applied. Use app.use(correlationIdMiddleware) to add it globally.
